feed.title: AI Wiki — Research Papers
feed.subtitle: New arXiv papers, triaged for relevance and summarised to key points.

entry.title: Repo-To-Skill: Distilling GitHub Repositories Into AI4AI Skills
entry.summary:
DisCo is a skill-powered research agent that distills operational knowledge from GitHub repositories into compact, reusable skills via task-agnostic and task-oriented methods.

Why it matters: Distilling repository code into compact, verified operational skills allows autonomous AI agents to dramatically improve ML research performance without expanding their context windows or compute budgets.

entry.title: SolarWM: Open Data and Scalable Training for Long-Horizon Video World Models
entry.summary:
SolarWM provides an open foundation for video world models, introducing a unified 1.43M-clip data engine and a three-stage training framework to deploy 5B–33B models capable of long-horizon rollouts.

Why it matters: It establishes a fully open, reproducible benchmark and pipeline that decouples multi-source video data preparation from diverse model architectures for scalable long-horizon world modeling.

entry.title: EarlyEval: Cheaper Agent Evaluation via Early Outcome Prediction
entry.summary:
EarlyEval reduces LLM agent evaluation costs by using lightweight LightGBM classifiers to predict task success or failure early and halt execution before completion.

Why it matters: It significantly lowers API costs and execution time during iterative agent benchmarking without requiring benchmark task distillation or sacrificing evaluation accuracy.

entry.title: It Takes Two to Match: Co-Evolving Generative Retriever with Reinforcement Learning
entry.summary:
CoGR is a retrieval framework that uses co-evolving reinforcement learning via GRPO to train LLMs to generate direct, aligned keyword representations for both queries and items, compatible with inverted indices.

Why it matters: CoGR enables LLM-driven generative retrieval across both queries and items without discarding existing, highly efficient keyword-based inverted index infrastructure.

entry.title: Language Models Can Control Their Own Attention
entry.summary:
Declarative Attention (DA) allows language models to dynamically declare required context regions within their chain-of-thought, enabling inference engines to skip reading unnecessary KV cache without extrinsic scoring.

Why it matters: It introduces a self-directed sparse attention mechanism that significantly cuts memory bandwidth and computational costs during long-context LLM decoding without retraining the model.

entry.title: On the Design Fundamentals of Pixel Text Representation Learning
entry.summary:
Pixel Linguist II introduces a native-resolution pixel-text encoder trained on 280M examples using variable resolutions, natural image pairs, layout-aware rendering, and a two-stage multilingual curriculum.

Why it matters: It establishes essential design principles for training pixel-text encoders that generalize across resolutions and languages while drastically reducing visual token footprints.

entry.title: HarnessDev: Can LLMs Create and Evolve Their Own Agent Harness?
entry.summary:
HarnessDev is a new benchmark evaluating LLMs on their ability to create and iteratively evolve execution infrastructure (agent harnesses) from minimal seeds, measured by downstream task success and token efficiency across fixed runtime models.

Why it matters: It reveals that LLM-generated execution environments are viable for specific domains like ML experimentation, but current models struggle to auto-optimize stable, generalizable agent infrastructure.

entry.title: ZipTok3D: High-Fidelity 3D Tokenization with Compact Token Prefixes
entry.summary:
ZipTok3D is a 3D tokenizer that uses nested dropout training and an iterative Transformer decoder to enable high-fidelity 3D reconstruction from ultra-short, progressively informative global-token prefixes.

Why it matters: By drastically reducing token sequence length while maintaining high-fidelity reconstruction, ZipTok3D significantly lowers memory and computational overhead for 3D generative models.

entry.title: Aspire: Can Models Self-Evolve from Vague Goals?
entry.summary:
ASPIRE is a new benchmark for LLM self-evolution that evaluates an agent's ability to interpret vague goals and optimize model weights or harnesses without access to explicit downstream tasks or metrics.

Why it matters: The benchmark demonstrates that current self-evolution methods struggle to generalize beyond explicit metrics, highlighting a critical gap in LLMs' ability to autonomously interpret broad human goals.

entry.title: Cliff: Learning Process Rewards from the First Mistake
entry.summary:
Cliff is a reward shaping strategy for RLVR that uses an off-the-shelf LLM teacher to detect the first mistake in a rollout and assign token-level advantages based on the correct prefix and incorrect suffix.

Why it matters: It provides fine-grained process supervision for LLM reasoning without the computational overhead of training specialized process reward models or relying on high-capability teacher models.

entry.title: S3Gym: Can LLMs Turn Self-Testing and Self-Judging into Self-Improvement?
entry.summary:
S3Gym is an interactive benchmark designed to evaluate LLM self-improvement by evaluating three coupled capabilities: Self-Testing, Self-Judging, and Self-Improvement across seven text-based games.

Why it matters: The benchmark reveals that LLM self-improvement is non-trivial, demonstrating that agents require mechanisms to transform feedback into executable policies rather than relying solely on experience accumulation.

entry.title: Influence-Directed Distillation: Solving the Diversity Bottleneck in Sampled-Token On-Policy Distillation
entry.summary:
Influence-Directed Adaptive On-Policy Distillation (IDA-OPD) resolves the diversity bottleneck in sampled-token distillation by using a First-Order Local Entropy Influence proxy to eliminate entropy-contracting updates without needing full-vocabulary teacher probabilities.

Why it matters: It enables student models to inherit teacher generation diversity and improve pass@k reasoning performance without incurring the high computational and memory costs of full-vocabulary teacher outputs.

entry.title: A Glance Is All You Need: Single-Pass Fine-Grained Image Captioning with SimLoss
entry.summary:
SimLoss enables fine-grained single-pass image captioning by aligning a vision-language model's hidden states with a frozen image embedding via InfoNCE loss without multi-stage pipelines or detailed text references.

Why it matters: It eliminates the 20x latency penalty of multi-stage captioning pipelines by recovering fine-grained visual details like textures, counts, and spatial relations in a single inference pass.

entry.title: Agents in the Large: Perception-Centered Architecture for Persistent Agents
entry.summary:
The Perception-Centered Architecture for Persistent Agents (Pera) provides a new framework for long-lived, adaptive language agents that continually construct lifecycle tasks from perception and control signals.

Why it matters: It establishes a theoretical and architectural foundation for building autonomous AI agents capable of continuous adaptation in dynamic, long-term user environments.

entry.title: VibeVoice-ASR-Streaming Technical Report
entry.summary:
VibeVoice-ASR-Streaming is an end-to-end, LLM-based streaming speaker-attributed ASR model that interleaves audio chunks, lookahead audio, and previous text for real-time transcription and speaker attribution.

Why it matters: It enables low-latency real-time voice assistants and agents to perform accurate speech recognition and speaker attribution simultaneously within a single end-to-end model.

entry.title: Language Models Can Control Their Own Attention
entry.summary:
Declarative Attention (DA) allows off-the-shelf language models to self-declare context retrieval regions within their chain-of-thought, reducing KV cache reads during decoding without fine-tuning.

Why it matters: It enables sparse attention during long-context decoding by leveraging intrinsic model reasoning rather than relying on external proxy scoring algorithms.

entry.title: LoRA-TSD: Tangent-Space Spectral Descent for LoRA via Muon-Style Updates
entry.summary:
LoRA-TSD optimizes LoRA parameters by performing Muon-style spectral-norm steepest descent within the low-rank weight matrix's tangent space and applying a native parametrization retraction.

Why it matters: It improves fine-tuning performance and rank robustness for large language models while reducing computational overhead compared to prior manifold-based optimization methods.

entry.title: oHC: Orthogonal Hyper-Connections on SO(4) via Quaternions
entry.summary:
Orthogonal Hyper-Connections (oHC) constrain residual mixing matrices to the SO(n) rotation group using unit quaternions, preventing gradient instability and stream similarity degradation without adding parameters.

Why it matters: oHC provides a faster, parameter-free mechanism to scale Transformers to multi-stream residual architectures while maintaining training stability and stream diversity.

entry.title: When Decodability Is Not Enough: Logical Validity Representations, Behavioral Dissociation, and Causal Tests in Language Models
entry.summary:
Researchers demonstrate that while logical validity is strongly decodable from the hidden states of open-weight transformers, this internal representation dissociates from behavioral accuracy and fails causal activation interventions.

Why it matters: The presence of decodable task information in a language model's internal representations does not guarantee that the model causally uses or behaviorally expresses that information during generation.

entry.title: Trace as State: Reasoning Traces as Conditional States for Long-Context Transformers
entry.summary:
Trace as State prepends generated reasoning traces before long-context blocks on a second pass, aligning task conditions with causal attention to significantly outperform post-context trace placement.

Why it matters: It enables substantial gains in long-context reasoning capabilities using existing causal transformer architectures without structural modifications.

entry.title: APEx: Distillation of Agent Procedural Experience for Adaptive Deep Research Question Answering
entry.summary:
APEx introduces a hierarchical experience utilization framework that distill agent interaction histories into category-level procedural skills to guide policy adaptation via alternating GRPO and test-time reinforcement learning.

Why it matters: APEx enables deep research agents to continually improve and adapt during deployment without requiring ground-truth labels or overloading context windows with verbose task traces.

entry.title: Breadth Beats Depth: Improving GCG-Based Jailbreak Optimization with Breadth-Oriented Suffix Search
entry.summary:
BOSS is a plug-and-play framework that enhances GCG-based jailbreak attacks by replacing deep greedy searches with a breadth-oriented suffix search using Tail-Focused Adversarial Loss.

Why it matters: By optimizing search trajectories and loss functions, BOSS makes white-box adversarial jailbreak generation against LLMs faster and more effective.

entry.title: Discriminative World Models for Web Agents
entry.summary:
Researchers introduced discriminative world models trained via predicted-state matching to generate web states that effectively distinguish correct actions from alternatives, improving web agent test-time action selection.

Why it matters: Aligning world model state predictions with downstream ranking mechanisms improves the accuracy of test-time search and action selection for autonomous web agents.

entry.title: Post-Training Language Models for Gold-Medal Performance in Coding Competitions
entry.summary:
An end-to-end post-training pipeline and test-time compute strategy trained Nemotron-3 models to surpass the top human score at the International Olympiad in Informatics (IOI) 2026.

Why it matters: This marks the first AI system to score higher than the top human contestant in an official International Olympiad in Informatics competition set.

entry.title: SafeEvolve: Harness-Policy Co-Evolution from Agent Experience for Safety Alignment
entry.summary:
SafeEvolve introduces an experience-driven framework that co-evolves runtime harnesses and agent policies using a two-stage SFT-RL paradigm to improve multi-step agent safety.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that concurrently updating external harness components and internal policy weights yields superior safety-utility tradeoffs compared to isolated safety alignment techniques.

entry.title: StudentSim: Training LLM-based Student Simulators
entry.summary:
StudentSim is a training framework that creates individualized LLM-based student simulators via pooled training and per-student specialization, outperforming GPT-5.4 in matching student behavior and responding to tutor guidance.

Why it matters: It enables the creation of highly personalized AI tutors by providing a high-fidelity proxy for real student learning without the need for slow and costly human trial data.

entry.title: Qwen-Drive-1.0: An Initial Step towards a Vision-Language Foundation Model for Autonomous Driving
entry.summary:
Qwen-Drive-1.0 is a vision-language foundation model for autonomous driving that unifies 3D perception, visual question answering, and motion planning into a single framework.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that standard vision-language models can be extended with explicit 3D perception and planning modules to handle autonomous driving without sacrificing general VLM capabilities.

entry.title: SMELT: Scaling Laws for Compute-Matched MoE Looped Transformers
entry.summary:
SMELT introduces compute-matched Mixture-of-Experts Looped Transformers that loop middle layers twice, outperforming standard MoE baselines and reducing compute-optimal training FLOPs by 6.8% to 18.0%.

Why it matters: SMELT proves that architectural looping offers true computational efficiency gains rather than just parameter savings, providing a practical method to reduce training FLOPs while improving downstream task performance.

entry.title: UI-Venus-2 Technical Report
entry.summary:
UI-Venus-2 is an open-source multimodal foundation GUI agent that unifies mobile, web, and desktop automation using a closed-loop reasoning-action framework and scaled RL verification.

Why it matters: It provides a unified, open-source foundation that improves the reliability, safety, and verifiability of digital task automation across diverse operating systems.

entry.title: ZimaBlue: Evolving Generalizable World Action Models through Scalable Video Pre-training
entry.summary:
ZimaBlue is a scalable World Action Model framework that leverages over 120,000 hours of egocentric video pre-training to improve zero-shot robotic manipulation success from 36.1% to 77.8%.

Why it matters: It demonstrates a practical method to convert abundant, action-free human and robot egocentric videos into real-time, highly generalizable control policies for physical robots.

entry.title: H3-World: Turning Language Understanding into World Control
entry.summary:
H3-World adapts the 33B MiniMax-H3 video generator into an interactive world model using temporal attention routing and lightweight LoRA fine-tuning.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that large video generators can be turned into precise, interactive world models with minimal parameter training by leveraging emergent language-based control.

entry.title: Hi-Q: Hierarchical Evidence-guided Query Refinement for Multi-Hop Question Answering
entry.summary:
Hi-Q introduces a dynamic, evidence-conditioned query tree framework that hierarchically refines multi-hop QA queries based on real-time corpus support rather than static templates or pre-built graphs.

Why it matters: Hi-Q improves multi-hop open-domain question answering performance without the heavy computational overhead of pre-constructing corpus-wide static graphs.

entry.title: Evaluating Multimodal LLMs as Generalist Vision-Language-Action Agents for Drone Control: Commanding, Approaching, Tracking and Searching
entry.summary:
The DroneCATS-Agent architecture and DroneCATS benchmark evaluate zero-shot Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs), from 2B parameter open models to frontier models, as direct drone-control agents across four core vision-language-action tasks.

Why it matters: Demonstrates that deploying zero-shot MLLM agents on edge hardware requires solving action protocol adherence and termination decisions rather than basic spatial navigation.

entry.title: Uncovering Understanding-Generation Synergy in Native Unified Multimodal Models: From Representation, Task to System
entry.summary:
Researchers systematically analyzed native unified multimodal models across representation, task, and system levels, discovering that task-decoupled architectures and end-to-end training unlock true synergy between visual understanding and generation objectives.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that native unified multimodal models can achieve functional synergy rather than performance tradeoffs when built with decoupled architectures and trained end-to-end.

entry.title: Safin-1: Safety from Within through Memory-Native State Evolution
entry.summary:
Safin-1 introduces Safety from Within, using a memory-routing architecture to maintain intrinsic, evolving safety capabilities directly within the model's native state.

Why it matters: It shifts model safety from external post-hoc constraints to an intrinsic, memory-native architectural property that adapts dynamically at test time.

entry.title: From Production Traffic to Post-Training: Building a Self-Hosted LLM That Covers the Corporate Request Mix
entry.summary:
Enterprises can consolidate diverse corporate LLM traffic onto a single self-hosted model by merging axis-specific GRPO experts via two-stage SLERP to avoid cross-domain reward interference.

Why it matters: This approach enables organizations under data-residency constraints to significantly reduce GPU infrastructure costs by replacing fragmented serving fleets with a single high-performing self-hosted model.

entry.title: Chain-of-Thought Faithfulness of Reasoning Models Varies with Where and How Preference Cues Are Delivered
entry.summary:
FACE-Eval reveals that LLM chain-of-thought faithfulness drops significantly when bias cues originate from tool returns or implicit raw artifacts rather than explicit user messages, making unstated preference adoption harder for external monitors to detect.

Why it matters: Chain-of-thought monitoring for AI safety and alignment becomes unreliable when models process implicit preferences via external tool outputs without explicitly reasoning about them in their output traces.

entry.title: DiagEvo: Diagnosis-Guided Self-Evolution via Hierarchical Error Memory
entry.summary:
DiagEvo enables LLM self-evolution by deriving a curriculum from solver failure history using a hierarchical error memory and double-confidence filtering, eliminating the need for external task resources.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that self-play models can continuously overcome specific reasoning weaknesses using self-generated failure diagnostics rather than relying on external datasets or human guidance.

entry.title: GUI-CC: Benchmarking Contextual Consistency of GUI World Models as Agent Environments
entry.summary:
GUI-CC is a benchmark evaluating the contextual consistency of GUI world models as multi-step agent environments rather than isolated single-step next-screen predictors.

Why it matters: It highlights that current GUI world models cannot reliably serve as simulation environments for training agents without addressing multi-step contextual decay.

entry.title: EM^2Mem: Event-Centric Multimodal Memory for Large Language Models
entry.summary:
EM^2Mem is an event-centric multimodal memory framework that binds heterogeneous evidence to event anchors during memory construction, resolving cross-modal and temporal fragment alignment issues in long-video question answering.

Why it matters: By providing generation-ready grounded event readouts instead of isolated fragments, the framework significantly cuts inference costs and latency while improving QA accuracy on long videos.

entry.title: When Safety Routing Breaks: Understanding Alignment Fragility under Benign Fine-Tuning
entry.summary:
A Fisher-geometric study reveals that benign fine-tuning breaks LLM safety by re-sharpening low-rank output-routing pathways in output-side MLPs, rather than through gradient conflicts.

Why it matters: Understanding safety loss as a disruption of low-rank output routing explains why LLM alignment is easily bypassed and guides better design of durable safety guardrails.

entry.title: Efficiently Estimating Optimal Hyperparameter Scaling Laws through Power-Law Entropy Search
entry.summary:
Power-Law Entropy Search (PLES) is a cost-aware multi-fidelity Bayesian optimization acquisition function that estimates optimal hyperparameter scaling laws for LLMs using under 10% of the compute budget required by grid search.

Why it matters: It enables machine learning teams to accurately predict optimal hyperparameter configurations for production-scale LLMs while cutting tuning compute costs by over 90%.

entry.title: Probing Factual Knowledge Transfer with Training Data Interventions
entry.summary:
An intervention-based framework using the SIFT benchmark shows that multilingual models transfer very little English-pretrained factual knowledge into Persian during continued pretraining, particularly for rare entities.

Why it matters: Multilingual models rely primarily on direct target-language exposure rather than cross-lingual transfer to retain factual knowledge, highlighting risks in assuming pretraining facts carry over across languages.

entry.title: The Structure of Quantization Damage in LLMs: Why the Next Bit Should Be Spent Globally
entry.summary:
Causal intervention on 9 LLMs shows quantization damage is diffuse, and spending extra precision on global finer granularity improves accuracy far more than selectively repairing localized critical layers.

Why it matters: When optimizing quantized LLM serving, hardware precision budgets should default to global granularity improvements rather than complex, selective layer-by-layer protection.

entry.title: Diffusion as a Training Curriculum for Timestep-Free Iterative Reasoning
entry.summary:
A timestep-free diffusion architecture with a persistent hidden state acts as an anytime solver that improves performance with inference depth and solves complex reasoning tasks without progressive denoising schedules.

Why it matters: This approach demonstrates that complex spatial and logical reasoning tasks can be solved through iterative noise-injection trajectories without relying on parallel rollouts, candidate selection, or external verifiers.

entry.title: SMELT: Scaling Laws for Compute-Matched MoE Looped Transformers
entry.summary:
SMELT introduces a budget-matched Mixture-of-Experts Looped Transformer recipe that loops middle layers twice, achieving higher compute efficiency than standard unlooped architectures.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that re-executing Transformer middle layers improves model performance and compute efficiency without increasing parameter count, memory footprint, or inference FLOPs.

entry.title: One-Layer Transformer Provably Learns Multiclass One-Nearest Neighbor in Context
entry.summary:
Researchers proved that one-layer transformers using standard argmax classification heads and simplex encoding are functionally equivalent to multiclass one-nearest-neighbor classifiers.

Why it matters: This theoretical proof grounds the in-context learning behavior of standard transformer architectures in well-understood nearest-neighbor classification mechanics for multiclass tasks.

entry.title: Post-Training Science for Supervised Fine-Tuning
entry.summary:
A systematic controlled sweep across Qwen3 and Llama models up to 235B parameters evaluates how SFT hyperparameter choices, optimizer selection, and dataset scaling impact downstream task performance.

Why it matters: It replaces empirical guesswork with measured, empirical rules for hyperparameter selection and tuning trade-offs during supervised fine-tuning.

entry.title: From Rollouts to Recipes: Self-Contained Post-Training for LLMs
entry.summary:
Self-Routing is a behavior-conditioned post-training framework that dynamically routes LLM training samples to GRPO, on-policy self-distillation, regularization, or skipping based on rollout correctness and confidence.

Why it matters: It improves LLM post-training efficiency and mathematical reasoning performance by adapting optimization strategies to sample difficulty without incurring extra annotation or sampling costs.

entry.title: When Tokenization is Secretly Output Supervision
entry.summary:
A controlled study reveals that tokenization functions primarily as output supervision in autoregressive models, where output granularity dictates task difficulty, training dynamics, and internal representations independently of input tokenization.

Why it matters: Cross-model evaluations may systematically reflect differences in task definition and supervision granularity rather than true underlying model capabilities.

entry.title: DreamX-Creator: Democratizing Native Audio-Video Generation at 2K Resolution
entry.summary:
DreamX-Creator 1.0 is a 7B joint audio-video generator producing synchronized 2K outputs via Gated Cross-Modal Attention, progressive pre-training, modality-aware reinforcement learning, and a 1-step autoregressive refinement pipeline.

Why it matters: It provides a compact, open-source 7B foundation for generating synchronized, high-resolution audio and video natively within a single model rather than relying on separate, cascaded systems.

entry.title: Does On-Policy Distillation Really Distill? From Noisy Teacher to Self-Improvement
entry.summary:
Analysis reveals on-policy distillation works primarily by suppressing low log-probability tokens rather than distilling teacher knowledge, motivating On-Policy Self-Adaptation, a supervision-free method that outperforms distillation.

Why it matters: Language models can achieve self-improvement and math performance gains without relying on external teacher models or dense token-level reward supervision.

entry.title: Lucida: Parse, Generate, and Place for Composable Real-to-Sim Scene Modeling
entry.summary:
Lucida introduces a composable real-to-sim pipeline that redistributes scene parsing, asset generation, and placement via GizmoAct, a vision-language model policy that aligns generated 3D objects using iterative GUI gizmo interactions.

Why it matters: Lucida enables the automatic creation of fully editable, high-fidelity 3D simulation environments from cluttered real-world video captures for embodied AI and robotics.

entry.title: Normalized Low-Rank Adaptation
entry.summary:
Normalized Low-Rank Adaptation (NoRA) stabilizes and accelerates parameter-efficient training by normalizing down-projection matrices during training or strictly at initialization.

Why it matters: NoRA offers a zero-overhead, highly scalable drop-in improvement for LoRA that accelerates convergence and enhances stability across multiple training paradigms.

entry.title: PaperGym: Rubric-Centered Evolution for Research-Plan Generation
entry.summary:
PaperGym converts research papers into RL training environments by synthesizing questions from goals/background and criteria from methods/experiments, reducing criterion leakage to 3.7%.

Why it matters: PaperGym provides a leak-resistant reinforcement learning environment and reward pipeline for training open-weights models to generate valid research plans without relying on verifiable answers.

entry.title: On the Design of Qwen3.8-Next Architecture: Evaluation, Efficiency, and Training Stability
entry.summary:
Qwen3.8-Flash-Next uses a 125B/6B-activated MoE architecture with Gated DeltaNet, Gated Residuals, and off-chip n-gram embeddings to outperform its 397B predecessor using 1/9th the training FLOPs.

Why it matters: The architectural and optimizer innovations drastically reduce training FLOPs and active parameter counts while maintaining benchmark performance and improving training stability.

entry.title: CogEvol: Towards Efficient and Reliable Learning Environment Generation
entry.summary:
CogEvol is a model family that generates structured-JSON slides and interactive HTML learning artifacts in a single pass using SFT and GRPO-based reinforcement learning.

Why it matters: CogEvol significantly reduces latency, compute costs, and hardware requirements for generating complex, interactive educational artifacts in production environments.

entry.title: LightNav-0: Eliciting VLM Spatial Intelligence for Generalist Embodied Navigation
entry.summary:
LightNav-0 is a compact, generalist embodied navigation model that unifies diverse navigation tasks by eliciting pretrained vision-language model (VLM) spatial intelligence using a token-based interface without task-specific prediction heads.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that compact VLMs can serve as unified, transferable backbones for complex embodied navigation, eliminating the need for task- or embodiment-specific architecture components.

entry.title: Scaling Large Reasoning Models beyond Human Supervision: A Path toward Superintelligence
entry.summary:
This paper presents a five-level taxonomy (L0 to L4) analyzing how large reasoning models can scale beyond human supervision across two dimensions: reward source evolution and experience generation.

Why it matters: It offers a structured framework for diagnosing failure modes and evaluating progress as reinforcement learning systems transition to self-sustaining, autonomous training regimens.

entry.title: Super Library Agent: Joint Generation and Maintenance of Multiple Applications Beyond the Single Codebase
entry.summary:
The Super Library Agent framework enables LLM agents to sequentially generate multiple related applications while automatically extracting reusable components into a shared Super Library to reduce code redundancy and structural erosion.

Why it matters: It enables LLM coding agents to maintain multi-application software portfolios efficiently without accumulating duplicate, dead, or structurally eroded code across repositories.

entry.title: Sliding-window beats linear attention
entry.summary:
Researchers demonstrate that Sliding Window Attention (SWA) with sinks performs as well as or better than post-trained Linear Attention models across multiple LLMs without requiring post-training.

Why it matters: Switching to SWA with sinks provides a cheaper, zero-training alternative to post-trained Linear Attention for reducing LLM inference memory costs.

entry.title: Evaluating the Hidden Costs of Personalization in Large Language Models
entry.summary:
Researchers introduced PRISK, a dynamic evaluation framework that revealed personalizing LLMs significantly degrades performance by increasing irrelevant personalization, preference narrowing, and sycophantic bias.

Why it matters: Conditioning LLMs on user history and profiles systematically degrades response objectivity and diversity, forcing a trade-off between user satisfaction and model bias.

entry.title: Learning to Evaluate Before Improving: Automatic Rubric Induction for Automatic Research Agents
entry.summary:
AutoSciRub is an evaluation-first framework for autonomous research agents that induces task-specific, verifiable rubrics before execution to guide experiments, verification, and iterative report revision.

Why it matters: It establishes a generalizable control mechanism that makes implicit experimental requirements explicit, preventing research agents from skipping crucial analyses or drawing unsupported conclusions.

entry.title: EvoUndo: Recoverability-Constrained Self-Evolution for LLM Agent Harnesses
entry.summary:
EvoUndo introduces a framework for verifying and synthesizing the recoverability of LLM agent self-evolution mutations across counterfactual states.

Why it matters: Iterative prompting is insufficient for safe self-modifying agents; reliable runtime self-evolution requires co-designed state grounding, verification, and expressive recovery languages.

entry.title: Lies We Can See: Joint Verbal and Non-Verbal Deception by VLM Agents in Embodied Social Interactions
entry.summary:
MineAmongUs is a 3D multimodal sandbox evaluated with the ARIA harness to benchmark joint verbal and non-verbal deception in VLM agents.

Why it matters: It establishes a benchmark for studying embodied VLM safety and alignment beyond text-only interactions, showing how non-verbal actions drive strategic deception.

entry.title: CARVE: Verified Expansion for Variable-Length Generation in Diffusion Language Models
entry.summary:
CARVE is a training-free decoding algorithm that enables variable-length generation in masked diffusion language models by dynamically expanding the canvas only when verified via counterfactual stability testing.

Why it matters: It eliminates the need to guess exact target output lengths prior to generation, reducing FLOP costs and preventing truncated output or degraded accuracy in diffusion LMs.

entry.title: HSRM: Hidden-State Reward Models for Test-Time Verification
entry.summary:
HSRM is a 2M-parameter hidden-state reward model that verifies LLM mathematical reasoning candidates by analyzing internal generator representations at step boundaries instead of re-processing solution text.

Why it matters: HSRM enables accurate test-time solution verification with significantly reduced computational overhead by recycling internal LLM representations already calculated during inference.

entry.title: A Model with No Head and Many Thoughts
entry.summary:
Soft Latent Thinking replaces the final vocabulary head with a lightweight projector, allowing autoregressive chain-of-thought reasoning in continuous embedding space instead of discrete tokens.

Why it matters: It lowers the computational cost of chain-of-thought reasoning while improving model performance by operating directly in continuous latent spaces.

entry.title: Does On-Policy Distillation Really Distill? From Noisy Teacher to Self-Improvement
entry.summary:
Analysis reveals on-policy distillation works primarily by suppressing low log-probability tokens rather than transferring teacher knowledge, inspiring On-Policy Self-Adaptation (OPSA), a supervision-free method that uses entropy-adaptive negative advantages.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that teacher models are unnecessary for on-policy distillation, enabling cheaper, supervision-free LLM self-improvement through token probability suppression.

entry.title: Faithfulness Is Not Free: Auditing Offline KV-Cache Quantization in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
entry.summary:
A study on offline KV-cache quantization in RAG reveals that INT4 compression severely damages response faithfulness—causing over 90% negative faithfulness shifts among correct answers—despite INT8 remaining near-lossless.

Why it matters: Deploying INT4 KV-cache compression in production RAG systems risks ungrounded hallucinations that standard accuracy benchmarks fail to detect.

entry.title: Low-Resource Preference Adaptation of LLMs via Activation-Based Label Propagation
entry.summary:
Researchers developed a method using lightweight linear probes trained on intermediate LLM activations from <=500 preference pairs to pseudo-label over 50k unlabelled examples for low-resource preference adaptation.

Why it matters: This approach enables efficient LLM alignment for non-mainstream, cultural, or highly personalized user preferences while drastically reducing expensive human annotation requirements.

entry.title: The Fragility of Jailbreak Robustness Across Operational States
entry.summary:
Jailbreak robustness evaluations using a default vanilla state fail to capture safety dynamics, as non-safety system prompts can alter attack success rates by up to 56 percentage points while shifting hidden representations along a refusal axis.

Why it matters: Single-configuration safety evaluations underestimate real-world risk, necessitating multi-state robustness benchmarks that account for benign variations in system prompts.

entry.title: BLOOM-WILT: Logit Tilting for Behaviour Elicitation in Automated LLM Auditing
entry.summary:
BLOOM-WILT is a black-box LLM auditing pipeline that combines cross-round auditor strategy revision with adaptive next-token logit tilting to efficiently elicit rare target model behaviors without additional training.

Why it matters: WILT significantly improves the sample efficiency of automated LLM safety auditing and can alter model safety rankings without requiring internal parameter access or fine-tuning.

entry.title: Reconciling Process Supervision with Outcome-Based Credit in Agentic Policy Optimization
entry.summary:
TASPO reconciles process supervision with outcome-based credit by converting privileged information into bounded, mean-preserving weights that redistribute trajectory-level RL advantages across executable actions.

Why it matters: It enables language-model agents to achieve fine-grained, action-level credit assignment from privileged training data without losing the reliable optimization signal of verified task outcomes.

entry.title: Wrong Prediction, Right Answer: Recovering Evidence from Collapsed LLM Sequence Scores
entry.summary:
A diagnostic protocol using a two-parameter target-label-free additive correction reveals that LLM reasoning failures often stem from output bottlenecks rather than absent internal logic.

Why it matters: Apparent zero-shot reasoning deficits in LLMs may reflect output expression failures rather than true capability gaps, requiring narrower interpretations of standard benchmark evaluations.

entry.title: LoopArena: Benchmarking Models as Runtime Controllers for Loop Engineering
entry.summary:
LoopArena is a benchmark evaluating AI models acting as Controllers that guide a separate, fixed Worker coding agent through long-running tasks across three evaluation settings.

Why it matters: It decouples the reasoning ability of runtime loop controllers from underlying coding agents, enabling targeted and cost-effective evaluation of long-horizon software engineering management.

entry.title: Beyond Data Scaling: Representation-Centric Continued Pre-training for Vision-Language-Action Models
entry.summary:
VLAct is a VLA backbone trained via representation-centric continued pre-training on heterogeneous multi-embodiment robot data, improving downstream performance under fixed data and compute budgets without relying solely on data scaling.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that optimizing representations during pre-training enables superior cross-embodiment transfer and task performance on a modest compute budget, reducing reliance on costly robot data scaling.

entry.title: Agentic Artifact Creation: Systems, Evaluation, Principles, and Opportunities
entry.summary:
A survey of 259 works introduces a framework for agentic artifact creation, defining stateful construction systems driven by operational representations, policies, and runtime verification feedback across six artifact families.

Why it matters: It provides a structured framework and evaluation principles to help engineers build reliable AI agents capable of producing complete, verifiable, and stateful deliverables.

entry.title: Code as Worlds: Agentic Discovery of Executable World Representations for Physical Reasoning
entry.summary:
Code-as-World introduces an agentic discovery paradigm that generates executable code to represent physical composition, dynamic evolution, and visual appearance from multimodal inputs.

Why it matters: It enables vision-language models to ground physical reasoning in controllable, quantitatively verified code abstractions rather than ungrounded visual approximations.

entry.title: J-Zero: Unified Challenger--Solver--Judge Co-Evolution from Zero Data
entry.summary:
J-Zero is a unified Challenger-Solver-Judge co-evolution framework that enables self-improvement across verifiable and unverifiable domains without human data.

Why it matters: It allows language models to continually self-improve without human supervision or ground-truth verifiers, mitigating degradation issues in complex domains.

entry.title: Revisiting Local Context for Long-Horizon Streaming 3D Reconstruction
entry.summary:
ABot-Recon achieves state-of-the-art long-horizon streaming 3D reconstruction using strictly local context without persistent long-range memory.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that maintaining complex long-range memory is unnecessary for stable, long-horizon streaming 3D reconstruction, significantly cutting memory requirements.

entry.title: LayerRecall: A State-Conditioned Memory Router for Long-Horizon Consistency in Video Generation
entry.summary:
LayerRecall is a current-conditioned memory router that selectively retrieves historical K/V states and injects them into specific memory-sensitive DiT layers to maintain long-horizon consistency in autoregressive video generation.

Why it matters: It enables autoregressive video diffusion models to reliably recall distant attributes and subjects across long time horizons without disrupting local continuity or adding computational overhead.

entry.title: ContextPilot: Teaching Agents for Proactive Context Management via Fine-grained RL
entry.summary:
ContextPilot is a proactive context management framework that enhances agent toolsets and uses fine-grained reinforcement learning to maintain compact working contexts in long-horizon tasks.

Why it matters: It enables LLM agents to execute complex, long-horizon tasks more efficiently by actively optimizing their context window size without losing critical information.

entry.title: Puro-2B: Poor Lab's Qwen2-1.5B Trained on RTX 5090 within $5090
entry.summary:
Puro-2B offers an Apache 2.0 open-source pretraining recipe using consumer RTX 5090 GPUs to train 2B-parameter models on 1.4T tokens for under $6.9K.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that competitive 2B-scale language models can be pretrained from scratch on consumer hardware within modest budgets, significantly lowering the financial barrier for academic and open-source AI research.

entry.title: Blind Men and the Elephant: Probing the Epistemic Myopia of LLMs under Long-Tail Divergent Knowledge
entry.summary:
Researchers introduced ElephantBench, a 1,094-question probe derived from low-exposure web corpora, to evaluate how well LLMs recall divergent accounts of long-tail facts.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that current LLMs suffer from epistemic myopia, systematically favoring dominant web perspectives while failing to retain valid minority accounts of long-tail knowledge.

entry.title: StepGuard: Learning Step-Level Guardrails with Scalable Supervision and Safety-Utility Balancing
entry.summary:
StepGuard is a step-level guard model that audits completed trajectories and pre-checks tool actions to defend LLM agents against unauthorized actions with minimal utility loss.

Why it matters: It enables real-time, pre-execution defense against malicious or risky tool invocations in LLM agent workflows without significantly degrading their problem-solving capability.

entry.title: Locate Anything in Videos: Rethinking Efficient Generative Spatio-Temporal Video Grounding
entry.summary:
Parallel Tube Decoding (PTD) replaces autoregressive trajectory serialization in spatio-temporal video grounding with a fixed 1+1 round generation process, dramatically reducing decoding latency.

Why it matters: PTD removes the latency bottleneck of autoregressive video trajectory generation, enabling fast, real-time spatio-temporal localization without sacrificing accuracy.

entry.title: Fast Weight Attention for Continual Learning
entry.summary:
Fast Weight Attention establishes read-after-write autoregressive semantics for recurrent fast-weight memories, introducing the Falcon algorithm family to improve online updates and length extrapolation.

Why it matters: It provides a mathematically grounded framework that unifies temporal alignment, plasticity, and bounded rehearsal to enhance context compression and extrapolation in recurrent sequence models.

entry.title: Paint What You See: Benchmarking Dexterous Visual Tool Use in Multimodal Agents
entry.summary:
Researchers introduced EASEL, a benchmark for fine-grained dexterous visual tool use, alongside the 440k-sample EASEL-Data curriculum dataset and the fine-tuned EASEL-9B model.

Why it matters: The benchmark exposes a systematic failure in current multimodal agents to translate fine-grained visual evidence into precise, parameter-driven physical or visual actions.

entry.title: Ring Forcing: Towards Precise Long-Term Memory for Autoregressive Video Diffusion
entry.summary:
Ring Forcing is an autoregressive video diffusion framework that enables precise long-term memory and minutes-long temporal coherence through a ring-structured training strategy, sequence compression, and sparse RoPE adaptation.

Why it matters: It resolves key long-term memory bottlenecks in autoregressive video generation, allowing models to maintain strict object permanence and identity consistency over minutes-long clips.

entry.title: VISTA: Verifier-Informed Student-to-Teacher Adaptation for On-Policy Self-Distillation
entry.summary:
VISTA enhances on-policy self-distillation by using outcome-verified rollouts to adapt the privileged teacher toward the student at top-k high-KL-divergence token positions, rather than treating the teacher as a fixed target.

Why it matters: It improves student reasoning accuracy in self-distillation frameworks without incurring additional sampling costs or complex auxiliary reward models.

entry.title: A Probabilistic Interpretation of KV Cache Eviction
entry.summary:
This paper formalizes KV cache eviction as a probabilistic expectation estimation problem, proving its computational hardness while introducing a sampling-based approach that enables decode-time correction for evicted entries.

Why it matters: Grounding KV cache eviction in probabilistic theory provides a principled framework to correct for dropped information during decoding, boosting LLM serving robustness without sacrificing compression gains.

entry.title: REINS: Refusal-Enhanced Inhibitory Steering with Sparse Autoencoder Features
entry.summary:
REINS is a dual-action SAE inference-time steering method that simultaneously suppresses harmful continuation features and enhances safe refusal features to prevent safety circumvention from complex prompt wrappers.

Why it matters: It provides a robust, lightweight inference-time safety mechanism that prevents models from being exploited by adversarial prompt wrappers while avoiding model collapse.

entry.title: DARTS: Decoder-Aware Representation Tuning via Surgery for Model Merging
entry.summary:
DARTS addresses representation bias in merged decoder LLMs using an entropy-weighted L1 loss and position-dependent additive bias terms, adding just 0.1% parameter overhead.

Why it matters: It enables accurate multi-task model merging for autoregressive decoder LLMs without full retraining or significant parameter overhead.

entry.title: VICT: Verifier-Instrumented Credit Tracing for Long-Horizon LLM Agent Reinforcement Learning
entry.summary:
VICT introduces verifier-side credit tracing for LLM agent reinforcement learning, assigning group-relative advantage along dependency-valid proof edges generated by terminal verifiers without using learned critics, process labels, or branch rollouts.

Why it matters: VICT provides an efficient mechanism for fine-grained credit assignment in long-horizon LLM agent training by extracting structural task evidence directly from existing code-based verifiers.

entry.title: Why Didn't It Check? Unsupported Final Claims and Their Repair in Two Tool-Equipped Language Models
entry.summary:
Tool-equipped language models can make unsupported final claims despite strict instructions, but providing missing evidence or applying automatic checking rules can repair 100% of these claims without degrading correct answers.

Why it matters: Enforcing targeted tool re-queries or automated evidence checks can systematically eliminate unverified model assertions without corrupting valid outputs.

entry.title: Fast Weight Attention for Continual Learning
entry.summary:
A new framework introduces Falcon-1 through Falcon-3 (and associated -A variants) to formalize fast weight attention updates using prefix-aligned read-after-write autoregressive semantics for continual sequence learning.

Why it matters: It enables recurrent sequence models to maintain robust performance in language modeling while enhancing length extrapolation on tasks like variable-digit addition.

entry.title: Blog: Survey of Optimizers
entry.summary:
A 2025-2026 survey categorizes neural network optimization across four design axes—temporal estimation, update geometry, horizon management, and systems representation—concluding that matrix-aware methods advance the field, though AdamW remains contextually irreplaceable.

Why it matters: It replaces single-optimizer hype with a compositional design framework and mandates stricter evaluation protocols across varied hardware and scaling constraints.

entry.title: Training Communication-Efficient Mixture-of-Experts Language Models with Layer Re-Configuration
entry.summary:
CE-MoE decouples token-mixing and channel-mixing depth by concentrating expert capacity into fewer routed MoE layers and adding dense layers, reducing training communication overhead without sacrificing performance.

Why it matters: It significantly reduces compute costs and training time for large MoE language models while boosting inference throughput without degrading model quality.

entry.title: How Proper Scoring Rules Shape LLM Forecasting
entry.summary:
Evaluating five proper scoring rules as LLM training objectives for binary event forecasting reveals distinct differences in calibration, error structure, and probability usage despite identical theoretical incentives.

Why it matters: Selecting a specific proper scoring rule as a training objective actively shapes the structural profile of an LLM's forecasting errors, meaning these loss functions are not functionally interchangeable in practice.
